newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Most Hungary BCE grain prices down, outlook mixed.
newsitem.headline: Most Hungary BCE grain prices down, outlook mixed.

text.p: Grain futures prices dropped for the third consecutive day on the Budapest Commidty Exchange (BCE) and traders saw mixed outlooks for the next week.
"Most of this week's price movements were speculative so there is almost no firm indication for the next days," said Sandor Torok of Agrokont.
Maize prices dropped further on Friday but only the May to October maturities saw the maximum permitted downward movement of 400 forints, with other deliveries easing by 300 to 380 forints.
"Nothing has changed in terms of available information to trade on," Torok said. "The surplus (of some one million tonnes) is still there".
He said prices, currently between 19,000 to 20,000 forints, could ease slightly over the next few days.
Milling wheat prices also dropped with old (1996) and new (1997) crop maturities moving together.
"This is a customary feature, only the nearest maturity tends to have a well-established market price," Torok said.
He added that recent speculation on how the cold weather would affect the crop is pointless.

"We can only expect realistic estimates by March," he said, but added that due to continuing demand, old crop prices - currently between 28,250 to 28,700 forints - could peak at around 30,000 forints.
Friday's total turnover was an unspectacular 397.1 million forints or 932 contracts, of which 737 contracts were for milling wheat.
Lot size is 20,000 kgs for all contracts.
